//: Which control planes this monitor can read, and how to reach each one.
Copy this file to ONE of these (first hit wins), and edit:
$KINERARY_FLEET_CONFIG
<hermes profile>/fleet-stacks.json        <- beside the skill, not inside it
~/.config/kinerary/fleet-stacks.json
It is kept OUT of the skill directory on purpose: install-hermes-skill.sh
diffs the skill, so a real deployment's config living inside it would show
up forever as drift against the repo.
Every stack needs a label and reachability. 'production': true marks the
one that describes real travellers; the agent is told never to merge its
numbers with anything else. 'default_stack' is what tools read when no
stack is named.
Three ways to reach a database, in increasing distance:
url        psql connects directly (managed Postgres, or a published port)
container  the database is in a container on this machine
ssh        ... and that machine is reached over SSH first
Anything stranger: 'argv' takes a literal command line, where {sep} is the
field separator and {pgoptions} the read-only connection options.
Binaries are found on PATH, with FLEET_SSH_BIN / FLEET_DOCKER_BIN /
FLEET_PSQL_BIN / FLEET_SH_BIN as overrides. Nothing here hardcodes a path.
'hermes_logs_dir' (optional) turns on the 'statistics' tool's tool-usage
section: an absolute path, on the host this stack's 'ssh' block reaches (or
on this machine directly if there is no 'ssh' block), to the PARENT
directory holding one subdirectory per Hermes profile, each with
logs/agent.log[.N] inside. It is an interim, log-derived source (approved
2026-09-28, to be dropped once a proper Hermes-hook pipeline exists) — read
with the same 'ssh' plumbing as the database (sudo unless ssh.sudo is
false), never through psql. Absent on a stack means tool usage is simply
not configured there; the statistics tool says so in words rather than
showing zeros.
Every <angle-bracket> value is a placeholder. Real hosts, container names
and key names belong in the private deployment config, never in this repo.

prod.label: production
prod.hermes_logs_dir: <absolute path on the control-plane host to the parent of the per-profile Hermes log dirs — optional, omit to leave tool usage unconfigured>
